prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Green Party Manifesto 2005 — Summary

Vision and approach
- Build a sustainable, fair society based on social, economic and environmental justice.
- End privatisation/PPPs in public services; prioritise prevention, equity, and local democracy.
- Ethical foreign policy focused on peace, human rights and tackling root causes of conflict.
- Urgent action on climate change, shifting to renewables and efficiency.

Economy and work
- Reduce inequality via progressive income tax (higher bands over £50k/£100k) and more bands in Corporation Tax (40% for largest firms).
- Tax unearned wealth: reform Inheritance Tax (based on recipient), abolish National Insurance and recover via broader income tax.
- Pilot Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax and business rates.
- Replace VAT with revenue-neutral eco-taxes on resource use, pollution and waste.
- Promote economic localisation: community banks, credit unions, local currencies; oppose UK entry to the euro; reform WTO rules.
- Create green jobs through renewable energy, zero waste and sustainable transport; defend workers’ rights and reduce working hours.
- Measure wellbeing, not just GDP (e.g., ISEW/MDP).
- Introduce Citizen’s Income and Citizen’s Pension.

Energy and climate
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence: CO2 cuts of 20% by 2010, 50% by 2020, 85% by 2030.
- Replace energy taxes with a Carbon Tax tied to fuel carbon content; protect low users.
- 40% of energy from renewables by 2020; major investment in wind, solar, wave, and biogas.
- Cut demand: Warmer Homes Act, Smart Energy Councils; transform transport.
- End nuclear: decommission at end of life; shift nuclear R&D to renewables.

Welfare, health, education, housing
- Phase in Citizen’s Income (simplify/replace means-tested benefits) and a universal Citizen’s Pension linked to earnings.
- Simplify and increase child support; end 48-hour opt-out and move toward 35-hour week; expand Sure Start.
- Boost social housing: let councils build, support self-build co-ops, use LVT; upgrade insulation/efficiency.
- Restore NHS founding principles; oppose PPPs and GATS in healthcare.
- Abolish prescription, eye test and dental charges; expand mental health and prevention.
- Raise health funding to at least 9% of GNP and hypothecate an NHS Tax.
- Increase education funding; scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; abolish SATs; individual learning plans; expand pre-school.

Transport
- Prioritise walking, cycling, public transport; cut road traffic 10% by 2010; shift £30bn from roads to public transport; re-regulate buses.
- Return rail and Tube to public ownership; expand rail, freight, light rail.
- Price true motoring costs: congestion/road pricing, higher fuel duty, abolish car tax disc; support clean-vehicle R&D.
- Curb aviation: no new runways, ban night flights, EU aviation fuel tax, UK domestic emissions tax, higher APD.

Environment, food and farming
- Zero Waste Strategy: ban incineration; 60% domestic recycling by 2010; eco-taxes on harmful inputs; Environmental Protection Commission.
- Precautionary principle on GM, xenotransplantation, nanotech; oppose patents on genetic resources.
- Animal welfare: end live exports, ban battery eggs (incl. enriched), tougher broiler rules, ban fur imports, extend hunting bans, end vivisection.
- Organics Target Bill: 30% organic production by 2012; replace CAP/CFP with support for organics, local markets, biodiversity.
- Ban GM food; toughen supermarket Code of Practice and OFT scrutiny.

Crime and justice
- Prevent crime via better urban design, youth services, rapid repairs, community staffing; treat drugs as health issue; oppose ID cards.
- Strengthen community policing and accountability.
- Tighten gun laws: broad prohibitions, clear lethality threshold, single robust licensing, regulate deactivated guns.
- Expand restorative justice; combat hate crimes and violence against women; advance disability rights.

Democracy and international policy
- Oppose national ID cards.
- Empower local and regional government; PR for local and Westminster; elected House of Lords; written constitution; disestablish Church of England; limit monarchy’s roles.
- Campaign No to proposed EU Constitution; reform EU for transparency and democracy.
- Ethical foreign policy: withdraw from Iraq, support UN peacekeeping, cut defence to EU average, end arms export support, pursue Arms Trade Treaty, decommission nuclear weapons.
- Increase aid to 1% of GNI; cancel debts of 52 poorest countries; support Tobin tax and fair carbon finance.
- Reform UN (end vetoed permanent seats), IMF and World Bank.
- Reform/replace WTO with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade enabling localisation and fair trade.
- Humane asylum: uphold rights, allow work and benefits, independent appeals; ratify migrants’ rights convention; improve EU standards.
